title: Only taking longs above the 200 average made this NQ strategy 8 points more over ten years and took a third off the drawdown
author: person-person12
selftext:
Everybody repeats that you should only take longs above the moving average, and I always read that as the rule that makes you more money. I ran the same strategy both ways on NQ and the money came out almost the same.

What I ran: a break of the 20 candle high on NQ 15 minute candles, long only, ATR stop and target, one contract, $50,000 starting balance, commission and slippage charged against me on both sides of every fill. 2016-05-29 to 2026-03-31, which is 230,019 candles. The two runs are the same code with one condition added, price above its 200 candle average at the moment of entry.

**No trend filter:** 202.3% total, 3,048 trades, 40.9% winners, profit factor 1.11, worst drawdown **24.3%**.

**With the trend filter:** 210.9% total, 2,639 trades, 41.5% winners, profit factor 1.14, worst drawdown **16.5%**.

So the filter threw away 409 trades, about 13% of them, and ten years later the two balances are 8.6 points apart. The drawdown is where it showed up, 24.3% down to 16.5%, roughly a third off the worst stretch, with the win rate moving half a point.

The profit factor barely moved either, 1.11 to 1.14, so the trades it kept werent much better one at a time. I had both trade lists sitting in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) so I could read them side by side, and thats the whole story in those four numbers.

The reason I care about the drawdown half more than the return half is that 24.3% of a $50,000 account is $12,000 and theres no funded account on earth that lets you sit through that. Same entries, same exits, one line of condition, and one of the two versions is something you could actually get funded on.

Both sets of numbers are net of costs.
